assessment: This paper provides a fundamental account of the role associative learning plays in sensorimotor adaptation. In a compelling result, the authors show that by pairing movement-related feedback with conditioning cues in the form of neutral auditory or visual contextual cues can be used to differentiate between sensorimotor perturbations/states. This work nicely integrates multiple literatures surrounding the processes supported by the cerebellum and solves a long-standing puzzle of exactly how and when arbitrary cues can serve to shape motor adaptation.
